Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediCore Dynamics, Inc. Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jennifer Hale, CFO; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and Laura Kensington, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MediCore Dynamics achieved record results this third quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance:
1. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
2. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
3. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
4. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
5. New product launches and contribution to growth
6. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
7. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
8. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

Jennifer will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will update us on our technology advancements, and Laura will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. In the medtech space, this mix is a critical leading indicator of revenue quality, margin sustainability, and long-term growth visibility. Our business model is similar to industry leaders like Intuitive Surgical with its da Vinci ecosystem or Stryker's Mako robotics platform, where capital sales of high-cost systems like our flagship OmniFlex surgical robots and advanced imaging suites expand the initial installed base, but the annuity-like consumables stream from single-use instruments, disposable endoscopes, orthopedic implants, and procedure kits delivers superior gross margins in the mid-70% range compared to the low-60s for capital.

In Q3, our overall revenue mix shifted favorably to 34% capital equipment and 66% consumables, up from 38% capital and 62% consumables in Q3 last year and improving sequentially from 36%/64% in Q2. This 400 basis point year-over-year improvement in the consumables tilt contributed about $28 million in incremental high-margin recurring revenue. By segment: In Robotics and Navigation, which is 42% of total revenue, capital sales grew 15% year-over-year to $112 million, driven by a surge in U.S. hospital capex budgets clearing post-COVID backlogs and the launch of our next-gen OmniFlex Xi+ system with enhanced AI-driven haptic feedback and 20% faster procedure times. Average selling prices held at $1.8 million per unit, with placements up 18% to 285 systems globally. Consumables here grew 28% to $210 million, fueled by a 12% increase in procedure utilization to 22 procedures per system per month, thanks to expanded single-use FlexiBlade instruments compatible with legacy systems. This segment's consumables mix reached a record 68%, highlighting the flywheel effect of our 1.2 million installed base.

In Cardiovascular and Endoscopy, 31% of revenue, capital was flat at 28% mix with $65 million from new cath lab imaging systems amid softer European hospital tenders due to reimbursement headwinds under the EU MDR framework. Consumables jumped 22% to $162 million, driven by volume growth in drug-eluting stents and disposable biopsy forceps, where ASPs rose 5% to $450 per unit on premium bioresorbable coatings. In Orthopedics and Spine, 27% of revenue, capital dipped to 42% mix as elective volumes normalized post-pandemic, but consumables grew 25% to $138 million via our Triad Implant System kits bundling cementless stems with navigation disposables, boosting attach rates to 92%.

Regionally: U.S., 62% of revenue, saw consumables at 70% mix, up from 65% year-over-year, supported by 14% robotic-assisted surgery growth per CMS data and stabilization under the No Surprises Act. Our direct sales expanded installed base penetration to 45% in top IDNs like HCA and Kaiser. EMEA, 22% of revenue, was capital-heavy at 45% mix due to delayed tenders in Germany and UK NHS, but consumables grew 19% on single-use device uptake amid infection control mandates post-Clostridioides difficile outbreaks. APAC, 12% of revenue, showed capital at 28% mix with China JDA approvals accelerating OmniFlex placements 35% year-over-year via state-owned hospital partnerships in Shanghai and Guangdong; consumables at 55% mix are ramping 30% with 40% localization of stents in Suzhou.

Strategically, we're optimizing this mix through technical innovation, including $180 million in R&D for ecosystem lock-in like RFID tracking for 95% compliance and predictive analytics via MediCore Cloud, lifting utilization 8% in beta sites. We're offering hybrid capital models like $2.5 million as-a-service leasing for emerging markets. Commercial execution via cross-selling boosted attach rates 15% in top 500 accounts, targeting 10% share gains in single-use endoscopy against Boston Scientific. This shift delivered consumables margins up 220 basis points to 74.5%, overall segment margins to 65.2%, up 180 basis points year-over-year. We see the mix trending to 30%/70% by fiscal year-end 2025, implying $1.2 billion recurring revenue run-rate and 200-300 basis points additional operating leverage with mid-single-digit procedure growth and stable FX. This de-risks our outlook amid high interest rates crimping capex.

Now, let's talk about SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. In med devices, SG&A typically runs 25-30% of revenue due to direct-touch sales for products like our Micra leadless pacemakers, Evolut PRO valves, and Hugo RAS robotic systems. We've deleveraged here amid inflation and reimbursement headwinds. For Q3, SG&A was $1.42 billion, up just 2% year-over-year but flat sequentially against 9% constant-currency revenue growth to $8.5 billion from 12% procedural increases in structural heart and 15% in diabetes with MiniMed 780G. As a percentage, it deleveraged 210 basis points to 25.4%, our lowest in five quarters. Year-to-date, up 3.5% to $4.1 billion or 26.1% of sales, down from 28.2%, with $180 million savings, 60% ahead of plan—outpacing peers like Boston Scientific at 27% and Abbott at 26.5%.

By bucket: Selling, 55% of SG&A at $780 million, grew 1% despite expanding to 12,000 reps for Hugo RAS at 250 systems placed, up 40%. G&A, 35% or $500 million, flat via back-office streamlining. Marketing declined 5% post-IDEFICS trial on Symplicity Spyral. Drivers: Sales force effectiveness with Veeva CRM and AI analytics boosting productivity 18%, targeting ICD upgrades 25% better, saving $45 million in travel. Right-sized territories post-$4.2 billion Affera acquisition saved $30 million annualized. G&A automation via UiPath RPA in Manila/Hyderabad cut invoice costs 32% to $8 each on $6 billion spend, unlocking $120 million working capital; SAP S/4HANA standardized contracts for 7% indirect savings, total $65 million year-to-date. Zero-based budgeting axed $25 million low-ROI marketing, shifting to virtual demos; procurement hit 85% compliance with hedges.

Regionally: U.S. 65% revenue at 27.2% SG&A due to 340B reserves but offset by tele-sales; Europe 20% at 23.8%, down 400 basis points via data lakes and IVDR normalization; emerging 15% at 18.5% with local hiring and e-commerce. This 'Precision Margin' framework trends SG&A to 24-25% by year-end, redirecting $250 million to Hugo RAS scaling, renal denervation, and M&A. Inflation in talent is watched, but 4.2x revenue per employee buffers. This delivers 300 basis points margin expansion, positioning for 12-15% EPS growth.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. R&D is the lifeblood in our competitive landscape with Boston Scientific, Abbott, and Intuitive Surgical, amid supply disruptions and reimbursement shifts. Q3 R&D was $285 million, 11.8% of $2.41 billion revenue, up 14% year-over-year and 5% sequentially; trailing 12-month at 12.2%, above 9-10% industry median. This supports 5.2% CAGR market growth from aging populations and minimally invasive shifts.

By area: 42% or $120 million to structural heart TAVR/mitral; 28% $80 million neuromodulation/diabetes CGM; 18% $51 million orthopedics/spine; rest endoscopy/digital. Efficiency up: 22% more patents at 156, pipeline ratio 1.8. Milestones: EvoFlex Ultra TAVR IDE enrolled 850 patients ahead, data Q1 FY2025 for PMA; Mitralis Pro TMVR 75% enrolled, 92% success. Percept PC neurostimulator breakthrough designation, 35% opioid reduction; LibreSense 3.0 CGM for CE Q4 2024, FDA H1 2025.

U.S. 52% spend leverages CMS bundles; KneeNav 2.0 NTAP status. Europe 28% MDR transitions; APAC 20% China JV low-cost TAVR. Tech: AI in 35% projects, robotics single-port, genomics. M&A like NeuroPace adds $35 million. FY2024 $1.15 billion R&D at 12%, to 13% FY2025 for $3 billion peak sales. Diversified pipeline mitigates risks.

Next, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Gross margin is key for operational discipline in devices with volatile resins and nitinol. Q3 GAAP 68.7%, up 150 basis points sequentially and 90 year-over-year; adjusted 69.4%, highest in five years, exceeding 67-68.5% guide, matching Boston Scientific.

Drivers: 80 bps mix from Watchman FLX Pro LAA at $12,000 ASP, 28% growth; 60 bps pricing 2-3% U.S. ortho like Persona IQ; 110 bps COGS—resins down 8%, yields to 96% Galway, $18 million vertical savings. U.S. 71.2%, EMEA 66.5% EtO pressures, APAC 72.1% Vietnam. Supply: 98.2% on-time vs 94% industry; diversified titanium suppliers Mexico/Europe, China to 18%; $150 million digital tech SAP/RFID; freight normalized. Target 70-72% 2025 with $250 million savings. Validates 'Innovate, Integrate, Insulate.'

Then, new product launches and contribution to growth. New products drove 42% of 18% revenue growth, NPP $285 million Q2 at 52% up, 22% total $1.3 billion. Half-year $540 million to $1.2 billion annual.

Standouts: VascuGuard Elite stent PMA Q4 2023, $112 million Q2 up 78%, 28% restenosis reduction ORBIT II; NeuroPulse Harmony AI neuromod $95 million, 62% headache reduction HELIOS; OrthoFlex AR knee $78 million, 98% accuracy ARTHRO-NAV. U.S. 68%, EMEA 48%, APAC 72%. 14% revenue R&D, M&A NeuroDyne. Guide 25% FY growth contribution. Positions 15-20% organic.

Then, key assumptions underlying the guidance. FY24 revenue $5.25-5.45 billion, 8-11% reported, 9-12% organic. Mid-single procedural: CV 7-9% TAVR, 10% WATCHMAN; ortho 6-8% ROSA; endoscopy 9-11%. U.S. 9-12%, Europe 5-7%, APAC 12-15%. FX 1% headwind. GM 67.5-68.5% mix/supply/pricing; OpEx SG&A 24-25%, R&D 12%. Macro GDP 2.2%, procedures 102% 2019. '3-3-3' framework.

Then, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter. Three pillars: innovation, commercial, resilience. Innovation: NovaPulse PFA IDE enrollment, NeuroFlex DBS MDR. Commercial: 15% rep productivity, U.S. TAVR 25%, EMEA 18%, APAC 35%. Resilience: CapEx $250 million, GM +200 bps. Q2 revenue $1.95-2.0 billion. M&A dry powder.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year. Q4 2024 $1.25-1.28 billion, 8-10% reported, 9-11% organic: CV/SH 12-14%, RAS 10-12%, EP 5-7%. U.S. 10-12%, EMEA 7-9%, APAC 13-15%. GM 66-67%, Op 24-25%. FY2025 $5.15-5.35 billion, 8-12% reported, 9-13% organic; GM 67-68%, Op 25-26.5%. Tailwinds NovaFlow, NovaCloud. Fortress balance sheet.

I will now turn the call over to Jennifer for a review of our financial results.

Jennifer Hale:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter. Q3 revenue reached $2.41 billion, up 12% organically, with adjusted EPS of $1.65, beating expectations. Expenses controlled tightly, profitability strong at 25% operating margins. Guidance incorporates the assumptions Alex outlined, with confidence in execution amid procedural tailwinds.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Jennifer. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, OmniFlex Xi+, is poised to transform the field of robotic-assisted surgery. We expect FDA approval in Q1 2025.

Building on Alex's R&D overview, our pipeline advances include EvoFlex Ultra TAVR pivotal completion, Mitralis Pro strong safety, Percept PC breakthrough, and LibreSense CGM clearances. KneeNav NTAP, China TAVR JV, AI/ML in 35% projects, robotics single-port. New launches like VascuGuard, NeuroPulse, OrthoFlex driving growth with premium margins and share gains. Digital twins accelerate submissions. This positions $3 billion peak sales.

Next, Laura with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Laura Kensington:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships are enabling us to access new markets and customer segments.

Echoing the mix trends, consumables optimization via cross-selling, attach rates up 15%, IDN penetration 45%. SG&A efficiencies boost rep productivity 18%, Veeva AI, territory optimization. Commercial acceleration: U.S. TAVR pull-through, EMEA ortho ramps, APAC China partnerships. New product ramps VascuGuard 78%, Harmony 110%. Regional: U.S. 68% new sales, APAC 72%. Share gains vascular 180 bps, neuro 220 bps. Priorities for next quarter align with Alex's pillars.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Laura. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee - JPMorgan:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the capital versus consumables mix, can you elaborate on the utilization drivers and how sustainable is the 70% consumables target by 2025?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, David. The 12% utilization increase to 22 procedures per system stems from FlexiBlade compatibility and MediCore Cloud analytics, up 8% in betas. RFID ensures 95% compliance. Sustainability comes from ecosystem lock-in, leasing models, and cross-selling—target 30/70 mix adds $1.2 billion recurring with procedure growth. Confident amid capex cycles.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. Regarding guidance assumptions, how sensitive is FY25 to FX or procedural slowdowns?

Jennifer Hale:
Emily, solid point. FX assumes 1% headwind at current levels—USD/EUR 1.08, JPY 150. Procedural baked mid-single with 10-12% CV/robotics tailwinds. Contingencies cover 2% volume risks like magnets. '3-3-3' framework plus share gains buffer to outperform 8% industry.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez - Morgan Stanley:
Appreciate it. On commercial priorities, any updates on APAC expansion and competitive dynamics?

Laura Kensington:
Yes, Mike. APAC double-digit with China 25% on NMPA/EvoValve localization—40% stents Suzhou, partnerships state hospitals. Japan fees add margins. Gaining vs Terumo/Lepu, OrthoFlex ASCs 28% mix. Rep productivity 15% lift targets share in TAVR 5%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Leerink Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim - Leerink Partners:
Thanks. For the pipeline, thoughts on AI integration risks and new launch contributions?

Raj Singh:
Sarah, AI/ML in 35% projects like Afib detection >98% sensitivity, endoscopy imaging. Risks mitigated by diversified late-stage 12 programs, 95% FDA timelines. New products 25% FY growth, VascuGuard coronary Q3 adds tailwinds. $1.15 billion R&D funds $3 billion peaks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
